sections.h2: Why Williston exteriors fail where they do
body: Look at almost any house in town and the wear tells the same story. The west and south faces chalk and fade first. The bottom foot of siding and door frames peel from splash-back. Shaded corners turn green. Exterior painting in Williston, FL has to answer all three, and that is why our walkthrough photographs every elevation separately instead of pricing the whole envelope at one rate.

Months of high summer humidity and frequent afternoon storms from June into September drive water into any open joint. Paint that is not bonded to sound wood or tight stucco lets that water in. For a closer look at the problem, read how humidity makes paint peel.

sections.h2: The prep sequence on a Williston exterior
bullets: Soft wash or pressure wash with mildew treatment
Scrape and sand failing coating back to a sound edge
Replace rotted trim and fascia; reset nail pops
Cut out cracked caulk and re-caulk moving joints
Mask glass, fixtures, drives, and plantings

body: Wood and fiber-cement siding and trim get 100% acrylic topcoats, which flex with heat and stay breathable. Stucco that shows hairline movement gets elastomeric, which bridges small cracks. Front doors, shutters, and railings get waterborne urethane enamel. We apply two full coats as the baseline and back-brush or back-roll sprayed areas where penetration matters. The product line is written on your estimate.
On farm properties, outbuildings and porches can be added as separate line items, each with its own system.

sections.h2: Older siding near downtown versus newer stucco and fiber cement
body: The prep list changes with the house. Older wood siding around the downtown core usually needs the most scraping and spot-priming, and sometimes board replacement. Newer homes along US-27 tend to have tight substrates but thin factory coatings, so the work shifts toward washing, caulk, and a thicker topcoat. See how this fits into the rest of our work on the Williston, FL location page, and read how long exterior paint lasts in Florida for realistic expectations.

Our preferred window runs October through May. Summer jobs still happen, but crews start earlier and watch the dew point and radar so fresh paint is not rained on. A typical full exterior takes three to seven working days plus wash and dry time. Each project carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, plus the manufacturer's coverage.
For the full process, see our exterior painting service. Many Williston clients also book pressure washing in Williston for the drives and walks while the crew is on site.

faqs.q: How long will an exterior repaint last in Williston?
faqs.a: It depends on exposure, substrate, and prep. Our article on exterior paint lifespan in Florida covers the main factors, and every exterior job we do carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years.

faqs.q: Can you paint in the summer in Williston?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. Crews start early, track dew point and radar, and stop before afternoon storms. October through May is still the best window.

faqs.q: Do you fix wood rot before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rotted trim and fascia are replaced during prep. Painting over soft wood only hides the problem for a short time.

faqs.q: Will you include my barn or shop building?
faqs.a: We can. Outbuildings are priced as separate line items with the coating system suited to their surfaces.
